passages.text: Then David asked, “Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?”
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David wanted to show kindness.
David remembered Jonathan, his friend.
David asked, “Is anyone still alive from Saul’s family?”
David said, “I want to show kindness to that person because of Jonathan.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד הֲכִ֣י יֶשׁ־ ע֔וֹד אֲשֶׁ֥ר נוֹתַ֖ר לְבֵ֣ית שָׁא֑וּל וְאֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה עִמּוֹ֙ חֶ֔סֶד בַּעֲב֖וּר יְהוֹנָתָֽן׃

passages.text: And there was a servant of Saul’s family named Ziba. They summoned him to David, and the king inquired, “Are you Ziba?” “I am your servant,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Saul had a servant.
His name was Ziba.
They called Ziba to come to David.
David was the king.
The king spoke to Ziba.
The king asked, “Are you Ziba?”
Ziba answered the king.
Ziba said, “I am your servant.”
passages.original: וּלְבֵ֨ית שָׁא֥וּל עֶ֙בֶד֙ וּשְׁמ֣וֹ צִיבָ֔א וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ ל֖וֹ אֶל־ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֵלָ֛יו הַאַתָּ֥ה צִיבָ֖א וַיֹּ֥אמֶר עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: So the king asked, “Is there anyone left of Saul’s family to whom I can show the kindness of God?” Ziba answered, “There is still Jonathan’s son, who is lame in both feet.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke.
David was the king of Israel.
David asked a question.
He said, “Is there anyone left from Saul’s family?”
He wanted to show God’s kindness to that person.
Ziba was a servant from Saul’s family.
Ziba answered the king.
Ziba said, “There is still a son of Jonathan.”
Jonathan was Saul’s son.
Ziba said, “He is lame in both feet.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ הַאֶ֨פֶס ע֥וֹד אִישׁ֙ לְבֵ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וְאֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה עִמּ֖וֹ חֶ֣סֶד אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ ע֛וֹד בֵּ֥ן לִיהוֹנָתָ֖ן נְכֵ֥ה רַגְלָֽיִם׃

passages.text: “Where is he?” replied the king. And Ziba said, “Indeed, he is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir son of Ammiel.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Ziba.
David asked, “Where is he?”
Ziba answered the king.
Ziba said, “He is in Lo-debar.”
Ziba said, “He is at the house of Machir.”
Ziba said, “Machir is the son of Ammiel.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ ל֥וֹ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֵיפֹ֣ה ה֑וּא וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הִנֵּה־ ה֗וּא בֵּ֛ית מָכִ֥יר בֶּן־ עַמִּיאֵ֖ל בְּל֥וֹ דְבָֽר׃

passages.text: So King David had him brought from the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
King David sent messengers.
King David ordered them to bring Mephibosheth to him.
Mephibosheth was Jonathan’s son.
Mephibosheth was staying in Lo-debar.
Mephibosheth was living at the house of Machir.
Machir was the son of Ammiel.
The messengers brought Mephibosheth from the house of Machir in Lo-debar.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֖ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ מִבֵּ֛ית מָכִ֥יר בֶּן־ עַמִּיאֵ֖ל מִלּ֥וֹ דְבָֽר׃

passages.text: And when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, the son of Saul, came to David, he fell facedown in reverence. Then David said, “Mephibosheth!” “I am your servant,” he replied.
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan.
Jonathan was the son of Saul.
Mephibosheth came to David.
Mephibosheth fell on his face before David.
Mephibosheth bowed down to David.
David spoke to Mephibosheth.
David said, “Mephibosheth!”
Mephibosheth answered David.
Mephibosheth said, “I am your servant.”
passages.original: וַ֠יָּבֹא מְפִיבֹ֨שֶׁת בֶּן־ יְהוֹנָתָ֤ן בֶּן־ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־ פָּנָ֖יו וַיִּשְׁתָּ֑חוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ מְפִיבֹ֔שֶׁת וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנֵּ֥ה עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: “Do not be afraid,” said David, “for surely I will show you kindness for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will restore to you all the land of your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table.”
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul.
David said, “Do not be afraid.”
David said, “I will show you kindness.”
David said, “I do this because of your father Jonathan.”
David said, “I will return to you all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul.”
David said, “You will always eat at my table.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ ל֨וֹ דָוִ֜ד אַל־ תִּירָ֗א כִּ֣י עָשֹׂה֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה עִמְּךָ֥ חֶ֙סֶד֙ בַּֽעֲבוּר֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן אָבִ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֣י לְךָ֔ אֶֽת־ כָּל־ שְׂדֵ֖ה שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַתָּ֗ה תֹּ֥אכַל לֶ֛חֶם עַל־ שֻׁלְחָנִ֖י תָּמִֽיד׃

passages.text: Mephibosheth bowed down and said, “What is your servant, that you should show regard for a dead dog like me?”
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and the grandson of Saul.
He came before King David.
Mephibosheth bowed down.
He spoke to David.
He said, “What is your servant?”
He asked, “Why do you notice someone like me?”
He called himself a dead dog.
He meant he was unworthy.
He wondered why David showed him kindness.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁתַּ֕חוּ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ כִּ֣י פָנִ֔יתָ אֶל־ הַכֶּ֥לֶב הַמֵּ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּמֽוֹנִי׃

passages.text: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “I have given to your master’s grandson all that belonged to Saul and to all his house.
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
Saul was the former king.
Ziba was a servant of Saul.
David called for Ziba.
David spoke to Ziba.
David said, “I have given everything that belonged to Saul to your master’s grandson.”
David included all that belonged to Saul’s family.
David gave all these things to Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֶל־ צִיבָ֛א נַ֥עַר שָׁא֖וּל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑יו כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה לְשָׁאוּל֙ וּלְכָל־ בֵּית֔וֹ נָתַ֖תִּי לְבֶן־ אֲדֹנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: You and your sons and servants are to work the ground for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master’s grandson may have food to eat. But Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, is always to eat at my table.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
passages.sermon:
King David spoke to Ziba.
Ziba was Saul’s former servant.
David said, “You must work the land for Mephibosheth.
You, your sons, and your servants will do this work.
You will bring in the harvest from the fields.
This food will provide bread for your master’s grandson.
Mephibosheth is your master’s grandson.
Mephibosheth will always eat at my table.
Ziba had fifteen sons.
Ziba had twenty servants.
passages.original: וְעָבַ֣דְתָּ לּ֣וֹ אֶֽת־ הָאֲדָמָ֡ה אַתָּה֩ וּבָנֶ֨יךָ וַעֲבָדֶ֜יךָ וְהֵבֵ֗אתָ וְהָיָ֨ה לְבֶן־ אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ לֶּ֙חֶם֙ וַאֲכָל֔וֹ וּמְפִיבֹ֙שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־ אֲדֹנֶ֔יךָ יֹאכַ֥ל תָּמִ֛יד לֶ֖חֶם עַל־ שֻׁלְחָנִ֑י וּלְצִיבָ֗א חֲמִשָּׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר בָּנִ֖ים וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדִֽים׃

passages.text: And Ziba said to the king, “Your servant will do all that my lord the king has commanded.” So Mephibosheth ate at David’s table like one of the king’s own sons.
passages.sermon:
Ziba was Saul’s former servant.
Ziba spoke to King David.
Ziba said, “I will do everything my lord the king commands his servant.”
Mephibosheth was the grandson of Saul.
Mephibosheth ate at King David’s table.
Mephibosheth ate like one of the king’s own sons.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר צִיבָא֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצַוֶּ֜ה אֲדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶת־ עַבְדּ֔וֹ כֵּ֖ן יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וּמְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת אֹכֵל֙ עַל־ שֻׁלְחָנִ֔י כְּאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica, and all who dwelt in the house of Ziba were servants of Mephibosheth.
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was the grandson of Saul and the son of Jonathan.
Mephibosheth had a young son.
His son's name was Mica.
Ziba was a servant of Saul's house.
Many people lived in Ziba's house.
Everyone who lived in Ziba's house served Mephibosheth.
passages.original: וְלִמְפִיבֹ֥שֶׁת בֵּן־ קָטָ֖ן וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מִיכָ֑א וְכֹל֙ מוֹשַׁ֣ב בֵּית־ צִיבָ֔א עֲבָדִ֖ים לִמְפִיבֹֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king’s table, and he was lame in both feet.
passages.sermon:
Mephibosheth was the son of Jonathan and the grandson of King Saul.
Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem.
He always ate at King David’s table.
Mephibosheth was lame in both feet.
passages.original: וּמְפִיבֹ֗שֶׁת יֹשֵׁב֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כִּ֣י עַל־ שֻׁלְחַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ תָּמִ֖יד ה֣וּא אֹכֵ֑ל וְה֥וּא פִסֵּ֖חַ שְׁתֵּ֥י רַגְלָֽיו׃פ
